title: Advocate 30min LLM SDK workshop skeleton
body:
Goal: 30 minute hands-on workshop advocates can run for product demos or community sessions. Emphasis: fast wins, clear failure modes, telemetry contract, and leaving attendees with a reproducible repo they can adapt.

Audience: developer advocates, APAC/EMEA friendly slot, audience has some JS or Python experience but new to Redwood SDK and production inference concerns.

Prereqs for attendees (what to ask them to do before the session):
- Install Node 18+ or Python 3.10+ (we'll provide both paths).
- Clone example repo: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples (branch: advocate-30m).
- Sign up for trial API key or use local proxy token (we'll provide ephemeral token for workshops).
- Optional: Docker if they want to run the local proxy (not required).

Materials to prepare (for host):
- Slide deck (6 slides) + speaker notes.
- Short repo with three lab folders: 01-hello, 02-telemetry, 03-rollouts. Include README with commands.
- Prebuilt ephemeral tokens and a small cheat-sheet with common errors and tips.
- A recording of the 30m flow for asynchronous follow-up.

Workshop agenda (30 minutes total):
- 0:00-02:00 (2m) — Welcome, outcomes. Quick poll: are you building chat, embeddings, or search?
- 02:00-08:00 (6m) — Live demo: basic text generation using Redwood SDK (JS). Explain API shape: client, model, prompt, streaming. Show latency and token cost quick metric on console.
- 08:00-18:00 (10m) — Lab time (attendees follow along):
  - Lab 1 (4m): hello-world generate — run a single request, switch model param, inspect response.
  - Lab 2 (6m): instrument telemetry contract — add a single line to capture request_id, model_name, prompt_length to console/trace. Show how SDK emits structured telemetry and how to map to Redwood Console.
- 18:00-26:00 (8m) — Failure and rollback scenarios (mini simulation):
  - Introduce flaky model variant (simulate slower 2s responses).
  - Show automatic fallback policy: call falls back to cheaper/shorter model with consistent API.
  - Exercise: attendees toggle a flag in config to force fallback and observe differences.
- 26:00-30:00 (4m) — Q&A, next steps, call to action (star the repo, join Slack channel, schedule office hours).

Speaker notes / key messages to weave in:
- Developer-first: same API across hosted / dedicated / private — show code parity briefly.
- Production realism: show how a single mis-sized batch or missing telemetry can double cost — quick anecdote.
- Observability: emphasize request_id and minimal telemetry contract (model, prompt_len, latency_ms, error_code).
- Rollouts: canary + automatic fallback keeps apps alive — show how to pin versions.

Repo walkthrough (what lives in each lab):
- 01-hello: minimal JS and Python scripts (examples/generate.js, examples/generate.py) with env var for REDWOOD_API_KEY. README commands: npm i, node examples/generate.js, python examples/generate.py
- 02-telemetry: small wrapper that logs structured JSON for each call. Telemetry snippet (JS): console.log(JSON.stringify({request_id, model, prompt_len, latency_ms}));
- 03-rollouts: config.json with model_priority list and a small script that simulates a slow model by sleeping, and an env toggle FORCE_FALLBACK=true that switches to the next model.

Commands and expected outputs (copy-paste friendly):
- npm i @redwood/sdk@local && node examples/generate.js
  - Expected: streaming tokens printed, final JSON with request_id, model_name, tokens: XX
- python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt && python examples/generate.py
  - Expected: single completion printed plus telemetry line to stdout

Failure injection scenarios (to demo reliability controls):
- Network latency: run local proxy with --delay 1500ms; show how SDK streaming still yields partial tokens and how client code degrades gracefully.
- Model OOM: simulate by returning 413 error from proxy; show how SDK surfaces error_code and how automatic fallback policy is triggered to next model.

Telemetry contract (opinionated minimal):
- request_id (uuid), model (string), model_variant (optional), prompt_len (tokens), tokens_generated, latency_ms, error_code (nullable), user_id (optional).
- Keep logs small and JSON-parseable for automatic ingestion into the Console.

Success metrics for the 30m workshop (for host to measure):
- 80% of attendees ran at least Lab 1 successfully.
- >= 50% added the telemetry snippet in Lab 2.
- At least 10% filed an issue or PR to the example repo within 48 hours.

Post-workshop follow ups (email template bullets):
- Thank you and links: repo, slides, recording, office hours sign-up.
- Quick checklist to try within 24 hours: change model param, add telemetry line, run fallback toggle.
- Ask for a volunteer to run a 1:1 15m pairing to integrate SDK into their project.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- Decide whether to ship JS-only or maintain both JS/Python parity for the lab (likely both but keep Python minimal).
- Add short Dockerfile for reproducible local proxy environment.
- Generate ephemeral tokens automation for public workshops (security review with security team).
- Prepare one-liner telemetry forwarder to map stdout JSON -> Redwood Console demo dataset.

Back pocket demo snippets (very short to rescue timing):
- Quick telemetry example (JS):
  const resp = await client.generate({model: 'rwd-small', prompt});
  console.log(JSON.stringify({request_id: resp.id, model: resp.model, prompt_len: prompt.length, latency_ms: resp.latency}));

- Quick fallback config (config.json):
  {"model_priority": ["rwd-small", "rwd-meduim-quant", "rwd-text-legacy"]}

Notes about tone and pace:
- Keep pace brisk, avoid deep infra talk. If audience asks about Dedicated/Private, offer a follow-up office hours slot.
- Use friendly, low-friction language — the point is to remove intimidation and create motion toward concrete integration.

Distribution plan after iterating:
- Publish as a GitHub template repo under redwood-inference/advocate-workshops.
- Small blog post with recording + quick checklist.
- Internal playbook with suggested advocates to run this in different regions (APAC-friendly times).

Revision history:
- 2025-03-12 initial skeleton (Aisha)
- 2025-03-15 added telemetry contract and failure injections (Marco)
- 2025-03-19 updated timing, TODOs, and linked artifacts (Priya)

Quick checklist for host before a session:
- Verify repo branch is clean and npm/pip installs are up to date.
- Create ephemeral tokens and test them.
- Run through slides and speaker notes once.
- Post the Slack invite link in the event chat 5 minutes before start.
